neighbours.label: the slot just before a word that states something evident or plainly wrong ('with an [injury]', 'what was [obviously]', 'your anxiety too [evident]'); the output promotes ' obviously', ' obvious', ' clearly'
fire: The striker was carried off in the second half with an injury to his knee.
Everyone in the room could see that the general was defending what was obviously a hopeless position.
Try not to make your disappointment too evident when the results are announced.
A wise reader learns to accept what is true and to reject what is false.
If you find a bird with an open wound, call the rescue centre.
The winger left the match early nursing an ankle injury.
If you think there is something wrong with your dog, take it to the vet.
The investors kept funding what was clearly a doomed venture.
quiet: The striker scored twice in the second half with a header and a volley.
Everyone in the room listened while the general described the new position.
Try to arrive early when the results are announced on Friday.
A wise reader keeps a notebook and writes in it every evening.
If you find a bird in your garden, put out some seeds and water.
The winger signed a new contract with the club on Tuesday.
If you have a dog, take it for a long walk every morning.
The investors met the founders at a hotel in Geneva.

notes: Card + look + 5 probe sentences (0.49-0.75 on 'what was', 'with an', 'nervousness too'; 0.04 on a plain 'the design was'). Broad pole (0.7% above 0.1 max), so near misses may fire weakly.
